stem: A car is moving in such a way that the distance it covers, is given by the equation \(s = 4t^2 + 3t\) where \(s\) is in meters and \(t\) is in seconds. What would be the velocity and the acceleration of the car at time \(t = 20\) second ?
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the book writes the acceleration step as \(a = \frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{dv}{dt}\right)\). That expression is the JERK (the third derivative of displacement); acceleration is \(a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{ds}{dt}\right)\). The operation actually carried out on the right-hand side is \(\frac{dv}{dt}\), and the printed answer \(8\) m/sec\(^2\) is correct.]

Let \(v\) be the velocity and \(a\) be the acceleration of the car.
Distance traveled by the car is given by
\(s = 4t^2 + 3t\)
Differentiate w. r. t. t.
\(\therefore\) Velocity of the car is given by
\(v = \frac{ds}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}\left(4t^2 + 3t\right) = 8t + 3\)   . . . (I)
and Acceleration of the car is given by
\(a = \frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{dv}{dt}\right) = \frac{d}{dt}\left(8t + 3\right) = 8\)   . . . (II)
Put \(t = 20\) in (I),
\(\therefore\) Velocity of the car, \(v_{t = 20} = 8(20) + 3 = 163\) m/sec.
Put \(t = 20\) in (II),
\(\therefore\) Acceleration of the car, \(a_{t = 20} = 8\) m/sec\(^2\).
Note : In this problem, the acceleration is independent of time. Such a motion is said to be uniformly accelerated motion.

stem: The displacement of a particle at time \(t\) is given by \(s = 2t^3 - 5t^2 + 4t - 3\). Find the time when the acceleration is 14 ft/ sec\(^2\), the velocity and the displacement at that time.
solution:
Displacement of a particle is given by
\(s = 2t^3 - 5t^2 + 4t - 3\)   . . . (I)
Differentiate w. r. t. t.
Velocity, \(v = \frac{ds}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}\left(2t^3 - 5t^2 + 4t - 3\right)\)
\(\therefore\) \(v = 6t^2 - 10t + 4\)   . . . (II)
Acceleration, \(a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}\left(6t^2 - 10t + 4\right)\)
\(\therefore\) \(a = 12t - 10\)   . . . (III)
Given : Acceleration = 14 ft/ sec\(^2\).
\(\therefore\) \(12t - 10 = 14 \Rightarrow 12t = 24 \Rightarrow t = 2\)
So, the particle reaches an acceleration of 14 ft/ sec\(^2\) in 2 seconds.
Velocity, when \(t = 2\) is
\(\therefore\) \(v_{t = 2} = 6(2)^2 - 10(2) + 4 = 8\) ft/ sec.
Displacement when \(t = 2\) is
\(\therefore\) \(s_{t = 2} = 2(2)^3 - 5(2)^2 + 4(2) - 3 = 1\) foot.
Hence the velocity is 8 ft/ sec and the displacement is 1 foot after 2 seconds.
